analysis.scope_and_question: Ebola virus disease (EVD) is a severe, often fatal zoonotic disease that continues to pose a serious public health challenge, especially in Central and West Africa. The review concludes that strengthening One Health platforms is critical for addressing EVD and other zoonotic diseases in the future.

analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on a comprehensive analysis of the literature, including the 2026 Bundibugyo virus outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and cross-border cases in Uganda. analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The 2014-2016 West African outbreak, initially reported in Guinea and subsequently spreading to Liberia and Sierra Leone, remains the largest EVD outbreak recorded to date, with more than 28,000 cases and 11,308 deaths. It also notes that currently licensed vaccines and monoclonal antibody therapies are only approved for Orthoebolavirus zairense, limiting treatment options during BDBV outbreaks. title: Serological and transcriptomic response of African fruit bats to immune challenge with recombinant vaccines expressing Ebola or Nipah virus antigens

analysis.methods: Antibody production was assessed using a Luminex-based multiplex microsphere immunoassay and a pseudotype virus neutralization assay, while transcriptomic analysis was conducted to evaluate gene expression changes in response to the vaccines.

analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings offer valuable insights into bat immune responses to filovirus antigens, which can inform the interpretation of serological data from wild bats and contribute to understanding the transmission dynamics of Ebola viruses.
